60:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Mumtahanah In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful The reason for the revelation of the beginning of this noble Surah was the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah. This Hatib was a man from the Muhajirun and also from the people of Badr. He had children and wealth in Makkah and was not from the Quraysh themselves, but was an ally of Uthman. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) decided to conquer Makkah after its people broke their covenant, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the Muslims to prepare to attack them and said, O God, make our report known to them. So this Hatib wrote a letter and sent it with the Quraysh to the people of Makkah, informing them of the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) intention to attack them, so that he might gain favor with them. God informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of this in response to his prayer. He sent after the woman and took the letter from her. This is explained in this hadith, the authenticity of which is agreed upon. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of his uncle, Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ali told me, Abdullah bin Abi Rafi told me and he said once that Ubayd God bin Abi Rafi told him that he heard Ali may God be pleased with him say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent me, Az-Zubayr and Al-Miqdad and said: Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter, so take it from her. So we set off, our horses galloping with us until we reached the garden, and there we saw the woman. We said: Bring out the letter. She said: I do not have a letter. We said: Bring out the letter or throw away the clothes. So she took the letter from her tie, and we took the letter and brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). In it was from Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah to some of the polytheists in Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Hatib, what is this? He said: “Do not rush me, for I was a man attached to the Quraysh, but I was not one of them. And those who were with you were from the Muhajireen, who had relatives who protected their families in Mecca.” So, since I missed that in terms of lineage among them, I wanted to take a hand among them to protect my kinship. I did not do that out of disbelief, nor out of apostasy from my religion, nor out of acceptance of disbelief after Islam. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has told you the truth. Then Umar said: Let me strike off the head of this hypocrite. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He witnessed Badr. How do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. This is how all the group narrated it except Ibn Majah through other chains of transmission on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. Al-Bukhari added in the Book of Military Expeditions: Then God revealed the Surah: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies. And he said in the Book of Interpretation: Amr said: And the verse: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies was revealed about him. He said: I do not know which verse is in the hadith or Amr said. Al-Bukhari said: Ali, meaning Ibn Al-Madini, said to Sufyan: It was said to him concerning this: Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies was revealed. Sufyan said: This is in the hadith of the people. I memorized it from Amr. I did not leave out a letter of it, and I do not know of anyone who memorized it except me. They both included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa`d ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me, Abu Marthad, and al-Zubayr ibn al-`Awwam, all of us on horseback. He said, Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman from the polytheists with a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah to the polytheists. We caught up with her walking on her camel to where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said. We said, The letter? She said, I have no letter with me. We made her kneel and searched for it, but we did not find any letter. We said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie. You must bring out the letter or we will strip you.” When she saw the seriousness, she rushed to her garment while she was protecting herself with a cloak, and brought it out. We went with her to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar said, “O Messenger of God, he has betrayed God, His Messenger, and the believers. Leave me alone so that I may strike off his head.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What made you do what you did? Hatib said: By God, I have no choice but to be a believer in God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. I wanted to have a hand with the people through which God would protect my family and my money, and there is none among your companions who does not have someone from his tribe through whom God would protect his family and his money. So he said: “He is truthful. Do not say anything to him except good.” Umar said: He has betrayed God, His Messenger, and the believers, so leave me to strike off his head. He said: Is he not one of the people of Badr? He said: “Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: ‘Do whatever you wish, for Paradise has been made obligatory for you,’ or ‘I have forgiven you.’” Umar’s eyes welled up with tears and he said: God and His Messenger know best. This is the wording of al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi about the Battle of Badr. It has been narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ali. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hasanjani told us, Ubayd ibn Ya’ish told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi told us on the authority of Abu Sinan, who is Sa’id ibn Sinan, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, on the authority of Abu al-Buhturi al-Ta’i, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to go to Mecca, he confided in some of his companions that he wanted to go to Mecca, among them Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah, and he spread among the people that he wanted to go to Khaybar. Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah wrote to the people of Mecca that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted you, so he informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me and Abu Marthad, and there was not a man among us who did not have a horse. He said: Go to Rawdat Khakh, for you will find a woman there with a book, so take it from her. So we set off until we saw her in the place mentioned by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). We said to her, Bring me the letter. She said, I do not have a letter. So we put down her belongings and searched her, but did not find it among her belongings. Abu Marthad said, Perhaps it is not with her. I said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not lie, nor did we.” We said to her, Either you bring it out or we will lend it to you. She said, Do you not fear God? Are you not Muslims? We said, Either you bring it out or we will lend it to you. Amr ibn Murrah said, So she brought it out from her room. Habib bin Abi Thabit said: I brought it out from before her, so we brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the letter was from Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah. Umar stood up and said: O Messenger of God, he has betrayed God and His Messenger, so allow me to strike his head. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did he not participate in Badr? They said: Yes. Umar said: Yes, but he broke his oath and supported your enemies against you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I am Seeing what you do. Umar’s eyes welled up and he said: God and His Messenger know best. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Hatib and said: O Hatib, what made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, I was a man attached to the Quraysh, and I had wealth and family there, and there was no one among your companions who did not have someone in Mecca to protect his family and wealth. So I wrote to them about that, and by God, O Messenger of God, I am a believer in God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hatib has spoken the truth, so do not say anything about Hatib except good. Habib bin Abi Thabit: Then God the Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection (Al-Baqara 2:17). And thus Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Abu Sinan Saeed bin Sinan, with his chain of transmission similarly. This was mentioned by the authors of Al-Maghari and Al-Seer. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in Al-Seerah: Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn Al-Zubayr told me on the authority of `Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr and other scholars of ours who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decided to march to Mecca, Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah wrote a letter to the Quraysh informing them of the matter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had decided to march against them. Then he gave him a woman. Muhammad ibn Ja`far claimed that she was from Muzaynah, and others claimed that she was Sarah, a slave girl of Banu `Abd Al-Muttalib. He gave her a reward to deliver it to the Quraysh. She put it in her hair and twisted her hair around it, then went out with it. report of what Hatib had done came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the sky. He sent `Ali ibn Abi Talib and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-`Awwam and said: Catch up with a woman with whom Hatib has written a letter to the Quraysh warning them of what we have decided to do with them. So they went out until they caught up with her at Al-Hulaifah, the ally of Banu Abi Ahmad. They made her dismount at Al-Hulaifah and searched in her saddlebags but found nothing. Ali ibn Abi Talib said to her, “I swear by God that the Messenger of God has not lied and we have not lied. Bring us this letter or we will expose you.” When she saw his seriousness, she said, Turn away. So he turned away. She untied the horns of her head and took out the letter from her and gave it to him. He brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called Hatib and said, O Hatib, what made you do this? Hatib replied, “O Messenger of God, by God, I am a believer in God and His Messenger. I have neither changed nor altered. But I was a man who had no family or clan among the people. I had children and family among them, so I treated them kindly.” Umar ibn Al-Khattab said, O Messenger of God, let me strike off his head, for the man has become a hypocrite. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, How do you know, Umar? Perhaps God looked at the companions of Badr on the day of Badr and said, Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. Then God, the Almighty, revealed about Hatib: “O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth. They expel the Messenger and yourselves [from the religion] because you believe in God, your Lord. If you have gone forth [to fight] in My cause and seeking My pleasure, [then] secretly [do] them affection, and I know what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way. If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you and stretch out against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve. Neither your wombs nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and God, of what you do, is Seeing. There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone.’” to the end of the story. Muammar narrated something similar from Al-Zuhri from Urwah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan mentioned that these verses were revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah that he said: He sent Sarah, the slave girl of Banu Hashim, and gave her ten dirhams. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, after her, and they caught up with her at al-Juhfah. He mentioned the rest of the story in a manner similar to what was mentioned above, and from al-Suddi something similar. And thus al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and more than one, that these verses were revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth. He means the polytheists and disbelievers who are at war with God, His Messenger, and the believers, whom God has made enmity and estrangement permissible, and He has forbidden them to take as allies, friends, and confidants, as God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever takes them as allies among you - indeed, he is [one] of them.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you or the disbelievers. And fear God, if you are believers.” And God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not take as allies the disbelievers rather than the believers. Do you wish to give God a clear authority over you?” And God the Almighty said: “Let not the believers take as allies the disbelievers rather than the believers. And whoever does that has no relation to God at all, except that you fear them out of fear. And God warns you of Himself.” That is why the Messenger of God May God bless him and grant him peace, he excused Hatib, when he mentioned that he only did that to please the Quraysh because of the money and children he had with them. Here we mention the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Mus`ab bin Salam told us, Al-Ajlah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Muslim, on the authority of Rib`i bin Harash, I heard Hudhayfah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us one, three, five, seven, nine, and eleven examples. He said: So he gave us an example of them and left out the rest. He said: “A people who were weak and poor were fought by people of tyranny and hostility. So God gave victory to the weak over them, so they turned to their enemy, used them, and gave them authority. So they incurred God’s wrath upon them until the Day they meet Him.” And the words of God the Most High: They expel the Messenger and you This, along with what preceded it of incitement to their enmity and lack of friendship with them, is because they expelled the Messenger and his companions from among them, disliking what they were upon of monotheism and devotion to God alone. For this reason, God the Most High said: That you believe in God, your Lord, meaning you had no sin against them except your belief in God, Lord of the Worlds, like His words the Most High: And they did not resent them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, and like His words the Most High: Those who have been expelled from their homes without right - only because they say, Our Lord is God. God the Almighty says: {If you have gone forth to strive in My cause and seeking My pleasure} meaning, if you are like that, then do not take them as allies. If you have gone forth striving in My cause, seeking My pleasure with you, then do not befriend My enemies and your enemies, while they have expelled you from your homes and your wealth out of spite and displeasure with your religion. God the Almighty says: {You do that secretly to them with affection, but I know what you conceal and what you declare} meaning, you do that, and I know what is in your hearts, your consciences, and your outward appearances. {And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the right path. If they gain control of you, they will be enemies to you and will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil} meaning, if they had power over you, they would not fear the harm they could inflict on you in words and deeds. {And they wish that you would disbelieve} meaning, and they are eager that you not attain any good. Their enmity toward you is both latent and apparent, so how can you befriend such people? This is also an incitement to enmity toward them. God the Almighty says: {Your kinship will not benefit you, nor your children, on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and God is Seeing of what you do.} Meaning, your relatives will not benefit you in the sight of God if God intends evil for you, and their benefit will not reach you if you please them in a way that angers God. Whoever agrees with his family in disbelief in order to please them has certainly failed and lost, and his work is in vain, and his kinship to anyone will not benefit him in the sight of God, even if he were a relative of one of the prophets. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: O Messenger of God, where is my father? He said: In the Fire. When he turned away, he called him back and said: Indeed, your father and my father are in the Fire. Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah with this chain of transmission.

They expel the Messenger and yourselves [from the religion] because you believe in God, your Lord. If you have gone forth [to fight] in My cause and seeking My pleasure, [then] secretly [do] them affection, and I know what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way. If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you and stretch out against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve. Neither your wombs nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and God, of what you do, is Seeing. There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone.’” to the end of the story. Muammar narrated something similar from Al-Zuhri from Urwah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan mentioned that these verses were revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah that he said: He sent Sarah, the slave girl of Banu Hashim, and gave her ten dirhams. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, after her, and they caught up with her at al-Juhfah. He mentioned the rest of the story in a manner similar to what was mentioned above, and from al-Suddi something similar. And thus al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and more than one, that these verses were revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth. He means the polytheists and disbelievers who are at war with God, His Messenger, and the believers, whom God has made enmity and estrangement permissible, and He has forbidden them to take as allies, friends, and confidants, as God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever takes them as allies among you - indeed, he is [one] of them.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you or the disbelievers. And fear God, if you are believers.” And God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not take as allies the disbelievers rather than the believers. Do you wish to give God a clear authority over you?” And God the Almighty said: “Let not the believers take as allies the disbelievers rather than the believers. And whoever does that has no relation to God at all, except that you fear them out of fear. And God warns you of Himself.” That is why the Messenger of God May God bless him and grant him peace, he excused Hatib, when he mentioned that he only did that to please the Quraysh because of the money and children he had with them. Here we mention the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Mus`ab bin Salam told us, Al-Ajlah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Muslim, on the authority of Rib`i bin Harash, I heard Hudhayfah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us one, three, five, seven, nine, and eleven examples. He said: So he gave us an example of them and left out the rest. He said: “A people who were weak and poor were fought by people of tyranny and hostility. So God gave victory to the weak over them, so they turned to their enemy, used them, and gave them authority. So they incurred God’s wrath upon them until the Day they meet Him.” And the words of God the Most High: They expel the Messenger and you This, along with what preceded it of incitement to their enmity and lack of friendship with them, is because they expelled the Messenger and his companions from among them, disliking what they were upon of monotheism and devotion to God alone. For this reason, God the Most High said: That you believe in God, your Lord, meaning you had no sin against them except your belief in God, Lord of the Worlds, like His words the Most High: And they did not resent them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, and like His words the Most High: Those who have been expelled from their homes without right - only because they say, Our Lord is God. God the Almighty says: {If you have gone forth to strive in My cause and seeking My pleasure} meaning, if you are like that, then do not take them as allies. If you have gone forth striving in My cause, seeking My pleasure with you, then do not befriend My enemies and your enemies, while they have expelled you from your homes and your wealth out of spite and displeasure with your religion. God the Almighty says: {You do that secretly to them with affection, but I know what you conceal and what you declare} meaning, you do that, and I know what is in your hearts, your consciences, and your outward appearances. {And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the right path. If they gain control of you, they will be enemies to you and will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil} meaning, if they had power over you, they would not fear the harm they could inflict on you in words and deeds. {And they wish that you would disbelieve} meaning, and they are eager that you not attain any good. Their enmity toward you is both latent and apparent, so how can you befriend such people? This is also an incitement to enmity toward them. God the Almighty says: {Your kinship will not benefit you, nor your children, on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and God is Seeing of what you do.} Meaning, your relatives will not benefit you in the sight of God if God intends evil for you, and their benefit will not reach you if you please them in a way that angers God. Whoever agrees with his family in disbelief in order to please them has certainly failed and lost, and his work is in vain, and his kinship to anyone will not benefit him in the sight of God, even if he were a relative of one of the prophets. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: O Messenger of God, where is my father? He said: In the Fire. When he turned away, he called him back and said: Indeed, your father and my father are in the Fire. Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah with this chain of transmission.
60:3: The reason for the revelation of the beginning of this noble Surah was the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. This Hatib was a man from the Muhajireen, and he was also one of the people of Badr. He had children and wealth in Makkah, and he was not from the Quraysh themselves, but rather he was an ally of Uthman. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) decided to conquer Makkah when its people broke the covenant, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the Muslims to prepare to attack them and said, O God, make our report known to them. This Hatib wrote a letter and sent it with the Quraysh to the people of Makkah, informing them of what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had decided to do to attack them, so that he might gain influence with them. God, the Most High, informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of this in response to his supplication, so he sent after the woman and took the letter from her. This is clear in this hadith, the authenticity of which is agreed upon. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of his uncle, Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ali told me, Abdullah bin Abi Rafi told me and he said once that Ubayd God bin Abi Rafi told him that he heard Ali may God be pleased with him say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent me, Az-Zubayr and Al-Miqdad and said: Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter, so take it from her. So we set off, our horses galloping with us until we reached the garden, and there we saw the woman. We said: Bring out the letter. She said: I do not have a letter. We said: Bring out the letter or throw away the clothes. So she took the letter from her tie, and we took the letter and brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). In it was from Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah to some of the polytheists in Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Hatib, what is this? He said: “Do not rush me, for I was a man attached to the Quraysh, but I was not one of them. And those who were with you were from the Muhajireen, who had relatives who protected their families in Mecca.” So, since I missed that in terms of lineage among them, I wanted to take a hand among them to protect my kinship. I did not do that out of disbelief, nor out of apostasy from my religion, nor out of acceptance of disbelief after Islam. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has told you the truth. Then Umar said: Let me strike off the head of this hypocrite. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He witnessed Badr. How do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. This is how all the group narrated it except Ibn Majah through other chains of transmission on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. Al-Bukhari added in the Book of Military Expeditions: Then God revealed the Surah: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies. And he said in the Book of Interpretation: Amr said: And the verse: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies was revealed about him. He said: I do not know which verse is in the hadith or Amr said. Al-Bukhari said: Ali, meaning Ibn Al-Madini, said to Sufyan: It was said to him concerning this: Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies was revealed. Sufyan said: This is in the hadith of the people. I memorized it from Amr. I did not leave out a letter of it, and I do not know of anyone who memorized it except me. They both included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa`d ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me, Abu Marthad, and al-Zubayr ibn al-`Awwam, all of us on horseback. He said, Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman from the polytheists with a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah to the polytheists. We caught up with her walking on her camel to where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said. We said, The letter? She said, I have no letter with me. We made her kneel and searched for it, but we did not find any letter. We said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie. You must bring out the letter or we will strip you.” When she saw the seriousness, she rushed to her garment while she was protecting herself with a cloak, and brought it out. We went with her to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar said, “O Messenger of God, he has betrayed God, His Messenger, and the believers. Leave me alone so that I may strike off his head.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What made you do what you did? Hatib said: By God, I have no choice but to be a believer in God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. I wanted to have a hand with the people through which God would protect my family and my money, and there is none among your companions who does not have someone from his tribe through whom God would protect his family and his money. So he said: “He is truthful. Do not say anything to him except good.” Umar said: He has betrayed God, His Messenger, and the believers, so leave me to strike off his head. He said: Is he not one of the people of Badr? He said: “Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: ‘Do whatever you wish, for Paradise has been made obligatory for you,’ or ‘I have forgiven you.’” Umar’s eyes welled up with tears and he said: God and His Messenger know best. This is the wording of al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi about the Battle of Badr. It has been narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ali. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hasanjani told us, Ubayd ibn Ya’ish told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi told us on the authority of Abu Sinan, who is Sa’id ibn Sinan, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, on the authority of Abu al-Buhturi al-Ta’i, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to go to Mecca, he confided in some of his companions that he wanted to go to Mecca, among them Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah, and he spread among the people that he wanted to go to Khaybar. Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah wrote to the people of Mecca that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted you, so he informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me and Abu Marthad, and there was not a man among us who did not have a horse. He said: Go to Rawdat Khakh, for you will find a woman there with a book, so take it from her. So we set off until we saw her in the place mentioned by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). We said to her, Bring me the letter. She said, I do not have a letter. So we put down her belongings and searched her, but did not find it among her belongings. Abu Marthad said, Perhaps it is not with her. I said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not lie, nor did we.” We said to her, Either you bring it out or we will lend it to you. She said, Do you not fear God? Are you not Muslims? We said, Either you bring it out or we will lend it to you. Amr ibn Murrah said, So she brought it out from her room. Habib bin Abi Thabit said: I brought it out from before her, so we brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the letter was from Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah. Umar’s eyes welled up and he said: God and His Messenger know best. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Hatib and said: O Hatib, what made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, I was a man attached to the Quraysh, and I had wealth and family there, and there was no one among your companions who did not have someone in Mecca to protect his family and wealth. So I wrote to them about that, and by God, O Messenger of God, I am a believer in God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hatib has spoken the truth, so do not say anything about Hatib except good. This was mentioned by the authors of Al-Maghari and Al-Seer. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in Al-Seerah: Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn Al-Zubayr told me on the authority of `Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr and other scholars of ours who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decided to march to Mecca, Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah wrote a letter to the Quraysh informing them of the matter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had decided to march against them. Then he gave him a woman. Muhammad ibn Ja`far claimed that she was from Muzaynah, and others claimed that she was Sarah, a slave girl of Banu `Abd Al-Muttalib. He gave her a reward to deliver it to the Quraysh. She put it in her hair and twisted her hair around it, then went out with it. report of what Hatib had done came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the sky. He sent `Ali ibn Abi Talib and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-`Awwam and said: Catch up with a woman with whom Hatib has written a letter to the Quraysh warning them of what we have decided to do with them. So they went out until they caught up with her at Al-Hulaifah, the ally of Banu Abi Ahmad. They made her dismount at Al-Hulaifah and searched in her saddlebags but found nothing. Ali ibn Abi Talib said to her, “I swear by God that the Messenger of God has not lied and we have not lied. Bring us this letter or we will expose you.” When she saw his seriousness, she said, Turn away. So he turned away. She untied the horns of her head and took out the letter from her and gave it to him. He brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called Hatib and said, O Hatib, what made you do this? Hatib replied, “O Messenger of God, by God, I am a believer in God and His Messenger. I have neither changed nor altered. But I was a man who had no family or clan among the people. I had children and family among them, so I treated them kindly.” Umar ibn Al-Khattab said, O Messenger of God, let me strike off his head, for the man has become a hypocrite. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, How do you know, Umar? Perhaps God looked at the companions of Badr on the day of Badr and said, Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. Then God, the Almighty, revealed about Hatib: “O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth. They expel the Messenger and yourselves [from the religion] because you believe in God, your Lord. If you have gone forth [to fight] in My cause and seeking My pleasure, [then] secretly [do] them affection, and I know what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way. If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you and stretch out against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve. Neither your wombs nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you, and God, of what you do, is Seeing. There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone.’” to the end of the story. Muammar narrated something similar from Al-Zuhri from Urwah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan mentioned that these verses were revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah that he said: He sent Sarah, the slave girl of Banu Hashim, and gave her ten dirhams. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, after her, and they caught up with her at al-Juhfah. Do you wish to give God a clear authority over you?” And God the Almighty said: “Let not the believers take as allies the disbelievers rather than the believers. And whoever does that has no relation to God at all, except that you fear them out of fear. And God warns you of Himself.” That is why the Messenger of God May God bless him and grant him peace, he excused Hatib, when he mentioned that he only did that to please the Quraysh because of the money and children he had with them. 60:4: God Almighty says to His believing servants whom He commanded to be sworn to, be hostile to, avoid, and disavow the disbelievers: There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him meaning, and his followers who believed with him “when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you’ meaning, we disavow you “and from whatever you worship other than God. We have disbelieved in you” meaning, in your religion and your way and there has appeared between us and you forever animosity and hatred meaning, enmity and hatred have been legislated from now on between us and you, as long as you are in your disbelief, we will forever disavow you and hate you until you believe in God alone meaning, until you believe in the Oneness of God and worship Him alone, with no partner or associate, and renounce what you worship along with Him of idols and rivals. And the Almighty said: Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you,’ meaning, in Abraham and his people you have a good example to follow, except for Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father. It was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. This was because some of the believers were praying for their fathers who had died as polytheists and asking forgiveness for them, and saying that Abraham was asking forgiveness for his father. So God Almighty revealed: “It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing.” God Almighty said in this verse: “There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have rejected you, and there has come between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone. ’ Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I do not possess for you anything from God. ’” That is, you have no example in that, that is, in asking forgiveness for the polytheists. This is what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ad-Dahhak, and others said. Then God the Almighty said, informing us of the words of Abraham and those with him when they left their people and disowned them, so they turned to God and beseeched Him, saying, Our Lord, in You we have relied, and to You we turn back, and to You is the final destination. That is, we have relied on You in all matters, and we have entrusted our affairs to You and delegated them to You, and to You is the final destination, that is, the return in the Hereafter. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve. Mujahid said: Its meaning is, do not punish us by their hands or by a punishment from You, lest they say, If these people had been on the truth, this would not have happened to them. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Qatadah said: Do not make them prevail over us, lest they tempt us with that, seeing that they only prevailed over us because of a right they had. Ibn Jarir chose this. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do not give them power over us, lest they tempt us. And the Almighty’s saying: “And forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” That is, conceal our sins from others and pardon them between us and You. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, that is, the One who does not wrong those who seek Your side. The Wise in Your words, deeds, law, and destiny. Then the Almighty said: Indeed, you have in them an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day. This is an emphasis on what came before, and what came before is also excluded from it, because this established pattern here is the first one itself. The Almighty’s saying: For whoever hopes in God and the Last Day, is an exhortation to that for every believer in God and the Hereafter. And the Almighty’s saying: And whoever turns away, that is, from what God has commanded, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, like His saying: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need, Praiseworthy. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Rich is the One who is perfect in His richness, and He is God. This is His description, and it is not appropriate for anyone but Him. He has no equal, and there is nothing like Him. Glory be to God, the One, the Compeller. The Praiseworthy, the One to be praised by His creation, meaning He is the One to be praised in all His words and actions. There is no god but Him and no Lord but Him.

So He commanded her to accept her gift and to let her into her house. Ibn Abi Hatim added to the period that existed between the Quraysh and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said: It is rejected in this context because Umm Aisha is Umm Ruman and she was a Muslim emigrant, and Umm Asma is someone else as is stated by name in these hadiths above, and God knows best. That is, He only forbids you from making friends with those who have declared enmity towards you, fought you, expelled you, and aided in your expulsion. God the Almighty forbids you from making friends with them and commands you to be hostile to them. Then He emphasized the threat against making friends with them, saying: And whoever makes friends with them - then it is those who are the wrongdoers. She was a Muslim, and he followed the religion of his people. When he was captured on the day of Badr, his wife Zaynab sent a necklace of hers that had belonged to her mother Khadija to ransom him. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw her, he felt very sorry for her and said to the Muslims: If you see fit to release her prisoner for her, then do so. They did so, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) released him on the condition that he send his daughter to him. He fulfilled his promise and was honest in his promise, and sent her to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with him. She stayed in Madinah after the Battle of Badr. She remained in Madinah after the Battle of Badr. Muawiyah married her, and Umm Kulthum bint Amr ibn Jarwal al-Khuza'iyyah, who was the mother of Ubaydullah. Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah ibn Ghanim, a man from his tribe, married her while they were still polytheists. Talhah ibn Ubaydullah divorced Arwa bint Rabia ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and after him, Khalid ibn Sa'd ibn al-'As married her. God the Almighty said: {And ask what you have spent, and let them ask what they have spent} meaning, demand what you spent on your wives who went to the disbelievers if they went, and demand what they spent on their wives who migrated to the Muslims. And the Almighty said: That is the judgment of God, which He judges between you, meaning in reconciliation and the exclusion of women from it, and the command to do all of this is the judgment of God, by which He judges between His creation. And God is Knowing and Wise, meaning He knows what is best for His servants, and He is Wise in that. Mujahid and Qatadah said: This is regarding the disbelievers who have no treaty, if a woman flees to them and they do not give her husband anything, then if a woman comes to them, nothing is given to her husband until he pays to the husband of the one who went to them the equivalent of his expenses on her. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: The believers acknowledged the judgment of God, so they paid what they were commanded to do of the expenses of the polytheists that they spent on their women, and the polytheists refused to acknowledge the judgment of God in what He imposed upon them of paying the expenses of the Muslims, so God the Almighty said to the believers in Him: “And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers, and you retaliate, then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they spent. And fear God, Who is Knowing and Wise.” You are believers in Him. If, after this verse, a believing woman were to go to the polytheists, the believers would return to her husband the maintenance he spent on her from the offspring in their hands, which they were ordered to return to the polytheists from their expenses, which they spent on their wives who believed and emigrated. Then they would return to the polytheists any surplus they had left. The offspring is what remained from the dowries of the disbelieving women when they believed and emigrated. Al-Awfi said that Ibn Abbas spoke about this verse, meaning that if the wife of a man from the emigrants joined the disbelievers, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would command that she be given the equivalent of what he spent from the spoils. Then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they spent meaning a dowry similar to hers. Ahmad also narrated it from the hadeeth of Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Umaimah with this chain of narration, and he added: And none of us shook hands with a woman. Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way from the path of Musa ibn ‘Uqbah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir with this chain of narration. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Abu Ja`far al-Razi from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: Umaimah bint Ruqayqah, who was the sister of Khadijah and the aunt of Fatimah, told me from her until he mentioned it. Imam Ahmad said: Ya`qub told us, my father told us, from Ibn Ishaq, Salit ibn Ayyub ibn al-Hakam ibn Salim told me, from his mother Salma bint Qays, who was one of the aunts of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and who prayed with him facing both qiblas. She was one of the women of Banu `Adi ibn al-Najjar, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to pledge allegiance to him with some women from the Ansar. When he stipulated that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor fabricate a lie between our hands and feet, nor disobey him in what is right, he said: And do not deceive your husbands. She said: So we pledged allegiance to him and then we left, and I said to one of the women, “Go back and ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) why he deceived our husbands.” She said: So I asked him, and he said: You take his wealth and favor others with it. Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Abi Al-Abbas told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Uthman bin Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Hatib told us, my father told me on the authority of his mother Aisha bint Qudamah, meaning Ibn Maz’un, who said: I was with my mother, Ra’itah bint Sufyan Al-Khuza’iyah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taking the women’s pledge of allegiance and saying: “I take your pledge that you will not associate anything with God, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill your children, will not bring forth a slander that you have invented between your hands and feet, and will not disobey me in what is right.” They said: Yes, as much as you are able. So they said: Yes, my daughter. So I said with them, and my mother said to me: Yes. So I said as they said. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Muammar told us, Abd al-Warith told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Hafsah bint Sirin, on the authority of Umm Atiyyah, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited to us, Let them not associate anything with God, and he forbade us from wailing. A woman withdrew her hand and said, So-and-so has made me happy, so I want to reward her. But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say anything to her, so she went and came back, and he pledged allegiance to her. Narrated by Muslim. In another narration: None of them fulfilled their promise except for her and Umm Sulaym bint Milhan. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Umm Atiyyah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a covenant from us when we pledged allegiance that we would not wail, and none of us fulfilled our promise except for five women.” Umm Sulaym, Umm al-Ala’, and the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Muadh, and two other women, or the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Muadh, and another woman. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pledge this allegiance to the women on the day of Eid, as al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim told us, Harun ibn Maruf told us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Jurayj told me that al-Hasan ibn Muslim told him, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “I witnessed the prayer on the day of Eid with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman. Each of them would pray it before the sermon, then he would deliver the sermon afterward. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came down, and it was as if I could see him when the men sat, with his hand in his hand. Then he came and separated them until he came to the women with Bilal, and said: ‘O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right,’ until he finished the entire verse. Then he said when he finished, ‘Are you all like that?’ One woman said: No one answered him but her: Yes, O Messenger of God. Al-Hasan does not know who she is. He said: Then give charity. Bilal spread out his garment and they began to throw the openings and the seals into Bilal’s garment. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Salim, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: Umaimah bint Ruqayqah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to pledge allegiance to him on Islam. He said: “I give you my allegiance that you will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children, nor fabricate a lie that you have fabricated between your hands and feet, nor wail, nor display yourselves like the display of the times of the first days of ignorance.” Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a gathering, and he said: Give me your allegiance that you will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children – he recited the verse that was taken from the women: When believing women come to you – “So whoever fulfills it, his reward is with God. And whoever commits any of that and is punished for it, it is expiation for him. And whoever commits any of that and God conceals it, it is up to God. If He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him.” Narrated by both of them in the Sahihs. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib on the authority of Marthad bin Abdullah Al-Yazni, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Abdul Rahman bin Asila Al-Sanabhi on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: I was among those who attended the first Aqaba, and we were twelve men, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took our pledge of allegiance as women took it, and that was before he imposed war, on the condition that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bring forth slander that we had invented between our hands and feet, and that we would not disobey him in what is right. And he said: If you fulfill it, then Paradise is for you. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Umar bin Al-Khattab, saying: “Tell them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, takes your pledge of allegiance that you will not associate anything with God.” And Hind bint Utbah bin Rabi’ah, who split open Hamza’s belly, was disguised among the women, so she said: If I speak, he will recognize me, and if he recognizes me, he will kill me. And I only disguised myself out of fear of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the women who… With Hind and Abin to speak, Hind said in disguise: How do you accept from women something that you do not accept from men? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) noticed this and said to Umar, Tell them not to steal. Hind said, By God, I sometimes commit sins against Abu Sufyan, and I do not know whether they are permissible for me or not. Abu Sufyan said, Whatever I have committed, whether in the past or in the future, is permissible for you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) laughed and recognized her. He called her and she took his hand and sought refuge with him. He said, Are you Hind? She said, God has pardoned what is past. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) turned away from her and said, nor should they commit adultery. She said, O Messenger of God, would a free woman commit adultery? He said, No, by God, a free woman does not commit adultery. He said, And they should not kill their children. Hind said, You killed them on the Day of Badr, and you and they are more perceptive. He said, nor should they bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet. He said, nor should they disobey you in what is right. He said, He forbade them from wailing. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to tear their clothes, scratch their faces, and cut their hair, and they would cry out for woe and destruction. This is a strange trace, and some of it is objectionable, and God knows best. When Abu Sufyan and his wife converted to Islam, the Messenger of God did not frighten them, but rather showed them sincerity and love, and this was also the case on his part, peace be upon him, towards them. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed on the Day of the Conquest. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) took the pledge of allegiance from the men on Safa, and Umar took the pledge of allegiance from the women beneath it, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). He mentioned the rest of it as mentioned above and added: When he said: And do not kill your children, Hind said: We raised them when they were young, and you killed them when they were adults. Umar ibn al-Khattab laughed until he lay down. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Nasr ibn Ali told us, Umm Ghubatah bint Sulayman told me, my aunt told me, on the authority of her grandmother, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Hind bint Utbah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to pledge allegiance to him. He looked at her hand and said: Go and change your hand. So she went and changed it with henna, then she came back, and he said: I give you my pledge that you will not associate anything with God. So she pledged allegiance to him, and she had two gold bracelets on her hand. She said: What do you say about these two bracelets? He said: Two embers from the fire of Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Aamer, who is Al-Shaabi, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, took the women to pledge allegiance while he was holding a cloth that he had placed over his palm. Then he said: And do not kill your children. A woman said: You will kill their fathers and you entrust us with their children? He said: After that, whenever the women came to pledge allegiance to him, he would gather them and present it to them. When they acknowledged it, they would return. So the words of God, the Most High: O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you means whoever among them comes to you pledging allegiance on these conditions, then he pledges her that they will not associate anything with God and will not steal the wealth of strangers. But if the husband is negligent in providing for her, then she is permitted to take from his wealth in a reasonable manner, as is customary among her peers, even if it is without his knowledge, in accordance with the hadith of Hind bint Utbah, who said: O Messenger of God, Abu Sufyan is a stingy man and does not give me enough money to support myself and my children. Is there any sin on me if I take from his wealth without his knowledge? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take from his wealth, in a reasonable manner, what is sufficient for you and your children. Narrated by both of them in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. God the Almighty said: And do not commit adultery is like His saying: "And do not come near adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way." In the hadith of Samurah, the punishment of adulterers is mentioned as painful torment in the fire of Hell. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Fatimah bint Utbah came to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he took an oath from her: Not to associate anything with God, nor to steal, nor to commit adultery the verse. He said: She placed her hand on her head out of modesty, and he was pleased with what he saw from her, so Aisha said: Recite, O woman, for by God, we only pledged allegiance on this basis. She said: Then yes. So he pledged allegiance to her on the basis of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Aamer, who is al-Sha'bi, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pledged allegiance to the women while he was holding a cloth that he had placed over his palm, then he said: And do not kill your children. A woman said: You kill their fathers and make a will about their children? He said: After that, when the women came to pledge allegiance to him, he would gather them and present it to them. If they acknowledged it, they would return. And the Almighty said: And let them not kill their children This includes killing them after they are born, as the people of ignorance used to kill their children for fear of poverty, and it includes killing them while they are fetuses, as some ignorant women do by aborting themselves so that they do not become pregnant, either for a corrupt purpose or something similar. God the Almighty said: {And let them not bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet} Ibn Abbas said: This means that they should not attribute to their husbands other than their children. Muqatil said the same. This is supported by the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud: Ahmad ibn Salih told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr told us, meaning Ibn al-Harith, from Ibn al-Haad, from Abdullah ibn Yunus, from Saeed al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say when the verse of cursing was revealed: “Any woman who introduces to a people someone who is not from them has nothing to do with God, and God will not admit her into Paradise. And any man who denies his child while he is looking at him, God will veil himself from him and disgrace him before the first and the last.” God the Almighty said: {And let them not disobey you in what is right}, meaning in what you command them to do of right and what you forbid them from doing of wrong. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Wahb bin Jarir told us, my father told us: I heard Az-Zubayr from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And let them not disobey you in what is right, he said: It is a condition that God has stipulated for women. Maymun bin Mihran said: God did not make obedience to His Prophet except in what is right, and what is right is obedience. Ibn Zayd said: God commanded obedience to His Messenger, and he is the best of God’s creation in what is right. Others have said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d, Abu Salih and others: He forbade them from wailing that day. The hadith of Umm Atiyyah on this matter has also been mentioned above. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding this verse, it was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a condition from them regarding wailing and not to speak to men except to a man among you who is a mahram. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: O Messenger of God, we have guests and we are absent from our women. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not those you meant, it is not those you meant. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Farra’ told us, Ibn Abi Za’idah told us, Mubarak told me, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Among the conditions the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took was that they should not speak to men unless she was a mahram, because a man would continue to speak to a woman until he ejaculated between his thighs. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Harun told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Umm Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, who said: Among the conditions the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stipulated for us regarding kindness when we pledged allegiance to him was that we should not wail. A woman from the Banu so-and-so tribe said: The Banu so-and-so tribe have made me happy, so I will not repay them. So she went and made them happy, then she came and pledged allegiance. She said: None of them fulfilled them. Other than her and other than Umm Sulaym bint Milhan, the mother of Anas bin Malik. Al-Bukhari narrated this hadith on the authority of Hafsa bint Sirin, on the authority of Umm Atiyah Nasiba al-Ansariyya, may God be pleased with her. A similar narration was also narrated from another source. He said: Ibn Jarir told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Nu`aym told us, `Umar ibn Farukh al-Qattab told us, Mus`ab ibn Nuh al-Ansari told me: I met an old woman of ours who was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: I came to him to pledge allegiance to him, and he took from us among what he took that we would not wail. An old woman said: O Messenger of God, some people had made me happy when misfortunes had befallen me, and now a misfortune has befallen them, so I want to make them the happiest. He said: Then go and reward them. So she went and rewarded them, then she came to him and pledged allegiance to him. He said: This is the good that God, the Almighty, said: And let them not disobey you in what is right. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, al-Qa`nabi told us, al-Hajjaj ibn Safwan told us, on the authority of Asid ibn Abi Asid al-Barad, on the authority of a woman among those who had pledged allegiance. She said: Among what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took from us was that we would not disobey him in what is right, that we would not scratch our faces, or tousle our hair, or tear our clothes, or cry out in woe. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told us, Ishaq bin Idris told us, Ishaq bin Uthman Abu Yaqub told us, Ismail bin Abd al-Rahman bin Atiyah told me on the authority of his grandmother Umm Atiyah, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) arrived, he gathered the women of the Ansar in a house, then he sent for us Umar bin al-Khattab may God be pleased with him. He stood at the door and greeted us, and we returned his greetings, then he said: I am the messenger of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to you. We said: Welcome to the Messenger of God and to the messenger of the Messenger of God. He said: Pledge allegiance that you will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery. We said: Yes. He extended his hand from outside the door or the house, and we extended our hands from inside the house. Then he said: O God, bear witness. He ordered us on the two Eids to go out, menstruating women and young women, and there is no Friday prayer for us. He forbade us from following funerals. Ismail said: I asked my grandmother about the words of God the Almighty: And let them not disobey you in what is right. She said: Wailing. In the two Sahihs, through the chain of transmission of Al-A’mash, from Abdullah bin Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is not one of us who strikes his cheeks, tears his garments, and calls out with the call of the Age of Ignorance. In the two Sahihs also, on the authority of Abu Musa, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disavowed the woman who strikes her cheeks, shaves her hair, and tears her hair. Al-Hafiz Abi Ya’la said: Hudbah bin Khalid told us, Abaan bin Yazid told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, that Zaid told him, that Abu Salam told him, that Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four things from the ways of the Age of Ignorance will remain in my nation and they will not abandon them: boasting about lineage, slandering lineage, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing over the dead.” He said: The female wailer, if she does not repent before her death, will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of scabies. Muslim narrated it alone in his Sahih, on the authority of Abaan ibn Yazid al-Attar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) cursed the woman who wails and the woman who listens to her. Narrated by Abu Dawud. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid, the freed slave of al-Sahba’, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And let them not disobey you in what is right, he said: The wailing. At-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir, on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd, on the authority of Abu Nu’aym, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Waki’, both of them on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah al-Shaybani, the freed slave of al-Sahba’, on the same authority. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib.
60:13: God Almighty forbids befriending the disbelievers at the end of this Surah, just as He forbade it at the beginning. God Almighty says: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry. Meaning the Jews, Christians, and all the disbelievers with whom God has become angry and cursed and who deserve to be banished and banished by God. So how can you befriend them and take them as friends and confidants when they have despaired of the Hereafter, meaning of the reward and bliss of the Hereafter, according to the judgment of God Almighty. And the Almighty’s saying: As the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves has two meanings: One of them is as the living disbelievers have despaired of their relatives who are in the graves meeting them after that because they do not believe in resurrection or revival, so their hope has been cut off from them in what they believe. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry to the end of the surah, meaning that whoever among those who disbelieved has died, the living have despaired of those who disbelieved ever returning to them or that God, the Almighty, will resurrect them. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, Just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves, meaning the living disbelievers have despaired of the dead. Qatadah said, Just as the disbelievers have despaired that the inhabitants of the graves who died will ever return to them. Ad-Dahhak said the same, and Ibn Jarir narrated them. The second statement means just as the disbelievers who are in the graves have despaired of all good. Al-A'mash said on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, Just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves, meaning just as this disbeliever despairs if he dies and witnesses his reward and learns of it. This is the statement of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Muqatil, Ibn Zayd, Al-Kalbi and Mansour, and it is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Mumtahanah. Praise and thanks be to God.
